standard_prerequisites.name: The endomorphism ring of a simple submodule
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies that the endomorphism ring of a simple submodule is a skew field.

standard_prerequisites.name: Rieffel's theorem
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies that the algebra coincides with the bicommutant of a right ideal, which identifies the algebra with the endomorphisms of the chosen module over the skew field.

core_obligations: The skew field (proof lines 366-369): choosing a simple submodule of the algebra as a module over itself, its endomorphism ring is a skew field by the cited lemma.

The identification of the algebra with an endomorphism ring (proof lines 370-372): Rieffel's theorem applied to that submodule shows that the algebra is the ring of endomorphisms of the module over the skew field.

The matrix algebra description (proof lines 373-375): since the module is finite dimensional over the ground field it is finite free over the skew field, so the endomorphism ring is a matrix algebra over the opposite skew field, which is the assertion.
proof_roadmap: Choose a simple submodule of the algebra and take its endomorphism ring.
Use Rieffel's theorem to identify the algebra with the endomorphisms of that module over the skew field.
Use finite dimensionality to write that endomorphism ring as a matrix algebra.
difficulty_reason: The theorem states that a simple finite algebra over a field is a matrix algebra over a finite skew field (statement lines 357-364). The proof is a complete argument: a simple submodule is chosen and its endomorphism ring is a skew field by a named lemma (proof lines 366-369); Rieffel's theorem identifies the algebra with the endomorphisms of that module over the skew field (proof lines 370-372); and finite dimensionality makes the module finite free over the skew field, so its endomorphism ring is a matrix algebra over the opposite skew field (proof lines 373-375). The non-formal content is the choice of the module and the freeness step. The claim is H2.
